title: Support for NSFs with psychosocial stressors and links to external partners
asked: Dr Haresh Singaraju asked whether, beyond the SAF's internal mental health support, full-time National Servicemen identified with mental health conditions linked to psychosocial stressors are systematically connected to external health and social sector partners to address triggers and support their well-being during and after service.
response: Mr Zaqy Mohamad said SAF identifies NSFs with psychosocial stressors through touchpoints such as Basic Military Training, surveys and commander interviews, and commanders can refer them to financial assistance, counselling or rehabilitation services. The SAF also works with MSF Social Service Offices and Family Service Centres, and MINDEF is piloting Case Connect to link medical professionals and social service offices for joint case management. He said he would take back to MINDEF a study on integrating better with the public health system, and would check on training for commanders and medical officers.

key_points.point: SAF identifies NSFs with psychosocial stressors through touchpoints such as Basic Military Training, surveys and regular commander interviews.
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: These NSFs are identified through various touchpoints during their service, such as the Basic Military Training, through surveys and regular commander interviews.

key_points.point: Support and referral options include SAF financial assistance schemes, counselling and rehabilitation services.
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: These include the SAF's financial assistance schemes, counselling as well as rehabilitation services.

key_points.point: The SAF works with MSF Social Service Offices and Family Service Centres to help those with added needs.
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: it works with the Ministry of Social and Family Development's Social Service Offices, and the community network of Family Service Centres to help those with added needs.

key_points.point: Most unit commanders overseeing NSF troops are trained and have schemes and mechanisms to support NSFs.
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: most of our unit commanders who oversee our NSF troops, for example, are trained and they do have schemes and mechanisms to support our NSFs

key_points.point: NSFs are encouraged to reach out to their commanders, the SAF Mental Health Office or the SAF counselling hotline.
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: We encourage NSFs who require assistance to reach out to their commanders, the SAF Mental Health Office or the SAF counselling hotline.

key_points.point: The SAF's collaboration with partners ensures continuity of support after NS.
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: So, doing so ensures the continuity of support for our NSFs after they complete National Service (NS).

left_open: Whether the linkage with external health and social sector partners is systematic across all NSFs identified with psychosocial stressors.
Whether education on psychosocial stressors and referral pathways is part of commander training or medical officer courses.
supplementary: Coordination between public healthcare and SAF, and whether commander and medical officer training covers psychosocial stressor referrals.
